claims.text: Ti28Ni28Fe14Al15Nb15 is a Ti–Ni-primary composition in which every element lies within the stated 5–35 at% range.
Conventional homogenization can produce a homogeneous, disordered state in the proposed Ti28Ni28Fe14Al15Nb15 alloy.
The proposed treatment consists of homogenization near 1150°C, cooling below 10°C/min to 750°C, holding for 10–20 hours, aging near 700°C for about 20 hours, and quenching.
Slow cooling to 750°C and holding for 10–20 hours will induce partial long-range B2- or L1₂-type ordering in the proposed alloy.
Aging near 700°C for about 20 hours will nucleate nanoscale coherent Nb-rich intermetallic precipitates in the proposed alloy.
The treatment will produce partially ordered superlattice domains embedded in a disordered matrix.
The treated microstructure will contain a fine dispersion of coherent nanoscale Nb-rich precipitates.
Ordered domains obstruct dislocation motion through superlattice strengthening.
Nanoscale coherent precipitates act as dislocation-pinning centers and provide precipitation strengthening.
Combining ordered domains and coherent precipitates will synergistically delay dislocation glide at elevated temperature.
Combining ordered domains and coherent precipitates will delay high-temperature creep deformation.
The treated alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than the same homogenized and rapidly quenched alloy.
The treated alloy will have a lower steady-state creep rate than the same homogenized and rapidly quenched alloy.
Rapid quenching after homogenization will produce a fully disordered control microstructure.
The rapidly quenched, fully disordered control will have lower high-temperature mechanical performance than the treated state.
The proposed microstructure is intended to remain useful for elevated-temperature service up to approximately 1150°C.
Prolonged high-temperature exposure may coarsen the precipitates or form undesirable brittle intermetallic phases.
Yield strength and steady-state creep rate measured at 800–1000°C can test the predicted mechanical improvement against an identically composed, rapidly quenched control.
Absence of a statistically significant yield-strength increase together with absence of a steady-state creep-rate reduction would falsify the hypothesis.
Formation of coarse or brittle phases that compromise ductility would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The procedure says to hold at 750°C and then 'reheat' to approximately 700°C; reaching 700°C from 750°C requires cooling unless an unreported intermediate cooling step occurs.
Compromised ductility is listed as a falsifying result, but no ductility measurement or acceptance criterion is included among the specified mechanical measurements.
